newsitem.title: UK: Scotia in drug accord with Japan's Ajinomoto.
newsitem.headline: Scotia in drug accord with Japan's Ajinomoto.

text.p: British drug discovery group Scotia Holdings Plc said on Tuesday it had signed an agreement with Japan's Ajinomoto Co Inc to develop a new drug for diabetes.
In a telephone interview with Reuters, chief executive David Horrobin said it would license SC103, a follow-up drug to Tarabetic, to Ajinomoto, which is Japan's largest food company.
Horrobin also told Reuters that he did not envisage a rights issue to fund the group's drug discovery programme "before next year or the end of this year".
Horrobin said the company had around 33 million stg in cash and 15 million stg of bank facilities. He said that in the first quarter, Scotia was burning cash at an annualised rate of 27 million stg.
"There is a substantial number of ways that cash could be raised" including agreements like that with Ajinomoto, sales of non-core assets and intellectual property, Horrobin said.
Under the agreement, Ajinomoto would have rights to market SC103 in Japan and a number of other Asian countries.

Scotia said it would receive an up-front fee and further milestone payments, although details were not disclosed. The company said there was significant potential for the drug in Japan, where there were six million diabetics.
SC103 is due to start Phase I clinical trials in Europe later this year, Scotia said.
Horrobin told Reuters that Phase II, or intermediate stage, trials would start at the end of 1997, and Phase III a year after that, with the drug potentially on sale in 2000 or 2001.

Scotia's first generation drug Tarabetic, for loss of nerve function and senstation loss suffered by diabetics, has run into problems with UK regulatory authorities. Horrobin said he was still confident that the product would be approved.
